'''Ruth Deborah Gates''' (March 28, 1962 – October 25, 2018) was the Director of the [[Hawaiʻi Institute of Marine Biology]] and the first woman to be President of the [[International Society for Reef Studies]]. Her research was dedicated to understanding [[coral reef]] ecosystems, specifically coral-algal symbiosis and the capacity for corals to acclimatize under future [[climate change]] conditions.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> Doctor Gates is most accredited with looking at coral biology and human-assisted coral evolution, known as ''super corals'', as notably seen in the documentary ''[[Chasing Coral]]'', available on [[Netflix]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Edmunds|first1=Peter J.|last2=Weis|first2=Virginia M.|date=January 2019|title=Ruth D. Gates (1962–2018)|journal=Nature Ecology & Evolution|volume=3|issue=1|pages=10–11|doi=10.1038/s41559-018-0763-4|pmid=30532049|issn=2397-334X|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Education ==
Gates was inspired by the documentary ''[[The Undersea World of Jacques Cousteau]]''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2016/04/18/a-radical-attempt-to-save-the-reefs-and-forests|title=A Radical Attempt to Save the Reefs and Forests|magazine=The New Yorker|last=Kolbert|first=Elizabeth|date=2016-04-18|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> She studied biology at [[Newcastle University]] where she earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1984.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://gatescorallab.com/ruth-gates|title=Ruth Gates|website=gatescorallab.com|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> She fell in love with corals during a diving trip to the [[West Indies]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.hawaiibusiness.com/20-for-the-next-20-2016/|title=20 for the Next 20: 2016|date=2016-03-03|work=Hawaii Business Magazine|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> In 1985 she moved to the West Indies to study corals.<ref name=":0"/> She completed her [[PhD]] at Newcastle University in 1989 on seawater temperature and [[algal]]-[[cnidaria]]n [[symbiosis]].<ref name=gatesphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Newcastle upon Tyne|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/18918380?style=html|title=Seawater temperature and algal-cnidarian symbiosis|first= Ruth Deborah|last=Gates|date=1989|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.346445}}|website=jisc.ac.uk|oclc=557254204}}</ref> During her postgraduate work in Jamaica, she was exposed to the bleaching response of coral resulting from rising temperatures.<ref name=":6">{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2018/nov/22/ruth-gates-obituary|title=Ruth Gates obituary|last=Brown|first=Barbara|date=2018-11-22|work=The Guardian|access-date=2019-11-29|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

==Career and research==
After her PhD, Gates was appointed a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref name=":1"/> Here she spent thirteen years working as a junior researcher in California, developing skills in cellular biology, evolutionary biology, and molecular genetics.<ref name=":6"/> She was there during the 1998 [[bleaching event]] that killed more than 15% of corals across the world.<ref name=":0"/>

Gates joined the [[Hawaiʻi Institute of Marine Biology]] in 2003.<ref name=":32">{{Cite web|url=https://www.tetiaroasociety.org/ruth-gates|title=Ruth Gates {{!}} Tetiaroa Society|website=www.tetiaroasociety.org|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> She studied corals and reefs, learning how they function and working on ways to slow their decline.<ref name=":32"/> She worked on [[Coconut Island (Oahu Island)|Coconut Island]], trying to identify why some corals survive bleaching.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/2012/03/corals-ocean-temperature/|title=Some Corals May Adapt to Warming Seas|magazine=WIRED|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> Her group monitored the ecosystems of coral reefs to understand how a changing environment impacted coral health.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=http://gatescorallab.com/monitoring-reefs|title=Monitoring Reefs|website=gatescorallab.com|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> The corals in shallow patches like [[Kāneʻohe Bay]] are subject to high temperatures and irradiance.<ref name=":4"/> Alongside seawater temperature, they measure photosynthetic active radiation, salinity and nutrient composition.<ref name=":4"/> This allowed them to build [[3D modeling|3D models]] of reefs.<ref>{{Citation|last=TheJohnburns84|title=Ke'ei|date=2015-10-28|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TxZLu7wByKY|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> They study the ''[[Symbiodinium]]'' that live within coral tissues. These provide the corals with energy and are lost during [[coral bleaching]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gatescorallab.com/symbiodinium-and-symbioses|title=Symbiodinium and Symbioses|website=gatescorallab.com|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> They develop new techniques for data analysis and management, including developing EarthCube and CRESCYNT.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gatescorallab.com/data-management-and-analysis|title=Data Management and Analysis|website=gatescorallab.com|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1440342|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1440342 – Earthcube RCN: Coral REef Science & CYberinfrastructure NeTwork (CReSCyNT)|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> Gates was concerned about [[sunscreen]] that contains [[octinoxate]] and [[oxybenzone]], and in 2015 called for it to be banned in Hawaii.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/clip/11941033/that-sunscreen-you-slather-on-it-might-be-damaging-coral|title=That sunscreen you slather on? It might be damaging coral|last=|first=|date=|website=Hawaii News Now|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> These sunscreens were banned in 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-05-04/hawaii-bans-sunscreen-coral-bleaching/9728322|title=Would you change sunscreen if it could help save the Great Barrier Reef?|date=2018-05-04|work=ABC News|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> In 2012 she demonstrated that the choice of symbiotic algae was crucial for how tropical reefs survived environmental stresses.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/discoveries/disc_summ.jsp?cntn_id=125278&org=NSF|title=Tropical Reefs Surviving Environmental Stresses: Corals' Choice of Symbiotic Algae May Hold the Key {{!}} NSF – National Science Foundation|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://app.dimensions.ai/details/grant/grant.2996203|title=A comprehensive survey of endosymbiotic and free-living Symbiodinium diversity in the corals and reef environments of Hawaii – Dimensions|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> She predicted that more than 90 percent of the world's corals will be dead by 2050.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/environment/environment-90-percent-coral-reefs-die-2050-climate-change-bleaching-pollution-a7626911.html|title=More than 90 percent of coral reefs will die out by 2050|work=The Independent|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref>

=== Gates Coral Lab ===
Gates established the Gates Coral Lab at the Hawaiʻi Institute of Marine Biology. Even after the death of Ruth Gates in October 2018, her team continues on to conduct research centered around the biological traits of coral reef ecosystems. The team uses their research to inform restoration efforts and management policies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gatescorallab.com/research|title=Research|website=gatescorallab.com}}</ref> Significant contributions to coral reef research has been contributed by the Gates Coral Lab. The team works in collaboration with the [[Australian Institute of Marine Science]] on the Coral [[Assisted Evolution]] Project, which attempts to "stabilize and restore coral reefs" in the face of climate change.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://coralassistedevolution.com/|title=Home|website=coralassistedevolution.com}}</ref>

Gates' research team hosted the first coral restoration workshop in Hawaii at the Hawaiʻi Institute of Marine Biology in 2017.<ref>Forsman ZH, Maurin P, Parry M, Chung A, Sartor C, Hixon MA, Hughes K, Rodgers K, Knapp ISS, Gulko DA, Franklin EC, Del Rio Torres L, Chan NT, Wolke CS, Gates RD, Toonen RJ (2018) The First Hawai‘i Workshop For Coral Restoration & Nurseries. Marine Policy 96:133–135. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marpol.2018.08.009</ref> The research team's restoration efforts in Hawaii's coral reefs focus on realistic and effective approaches. Recent publications have discussed the necessity of focusing on local restoration and recovery efforts as opposed to mass scale restoration until there is more substantial research on how to best combat the root of the problem of bleaching events, climate change.<ref>Ainsworth TD, CL Hurd, RD Gates, PW Boyd (2019) How do we overcome abrupt degradation of marine ecosystems and meet the challenge of heatwaves and climate extremes? Global Change Biology 26: 343–354 https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.14901</ref> Other research and restoration publications have discussed the effects of beneficial mutations, genetic variation, and human assisted relocation.<ref>Drury C. (2020) Resilience in Reef-Building Corals: The ecological and evolutionary importance of the host response to thermal stress. Molecular Ecology</ref>

=== Super Coral ===
"Super corals" were defined as those that did not bleach during natural bleaching events when sea temperatures were high.<ref name=":6"/> Gates identified these so-called "super corals" as a potential mechanism for preventing coral extinction.<ref name=":6"/> Gates said, "I just cannot bear the idea that future generations may not experience a coral reef. The mission is to start solving the problem, not just to study it."<ref name=":6"/> In 2013, she won the [[Paul G. Allen]] Ocean Challenge, a $10,000 prize that allowed her to improve the resilience of vulnerable coral reef ecosystems.<ref name=":52">{{Cite web|url=http://www.pgaphilanthropies.org/oceanchallenge/|title=OceanChallenge – Home|website=www.pgaphilanthropies.org|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pgaphilanthropies.org/news/news-articles/press-releases/press-release-the-paul-g-allen-family-foundation-n|title=Press Release – The Paul G. Allen Family Foundation Names Winner of Inaugural Ocean Challenge – Paul G. Allen Philanthropies|website=www.pgaphilanthropies.org|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> For the proposal, Gates joined [[Madeleine van Oppen]], and used genetic selection to boost resilience to environmental stress.<ref name=":52"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aims.gov.au/docs/media/latest-releases/-/asset_publisher/8Kfw/content/ocean-prize-for-assisted-coral-evolution|title=About the Australian Institute of Marine Science|author=Anon|website=www.aims.gov.au|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> They did this by exposing cross-bred corals to successively warmer and more acidic experimental tanks.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/09/20/climate/coral-great-barrier-reef.html|title=Building a Better Coral Reef|work=The New York Times|date=20 September 2017 |access-date=2018-10-28 |last1=Cave |first1=Damien |last2=Gillis |first2=Justin }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/environment/this-coral-must-die/|title=This coral must die|date=2018-07-06|work=The Seattle Times|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/hawaiian-coral-evolution-sparks-worldwide-debate|title=Hawaiian coral evolution sparks worldwide debate|date=2016-02-13|work=Times Higher Education (THE)|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/2016/05/scientists-can-engineer-climate-resistant-coral/|title=The Controversial Race to Breed Climate-Adapted Super Coral|magazine=WIRED|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> In the laboratory, they took resistant corals and collected their reproductive products after spawning, raised their offspring in the lab, and tested for increased temperature resistance.<ref name=":6"/> Gates was awarded the [[University of Hawaii]] Board of Regents Medal for Excellence in Research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hawaii.edu/about/awards/research.php|title=Regents' Medal for Excellence in Research :: University of Hawaii System|last=System|first=University of Hawaii|website=www.hawaii.edu|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> ''Coral Assisted Evolution, a'' $4 million research project, was funded by the [[Paul G. Allen Frontiers Group]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://coralassistedevolution.com/contact|title=Contact|website=coralassistedevolution.com|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> This supported Gates' research for four years from 2016, developing ''super corals'' that can withstand climate change.<ref>{{Citation|last=Vulcan Inc.|title=Innovator Profiles: Ruth Gates Is Working to Save Coral Reefs|date=2018-02-21|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pmxUXLb539o|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> Whilst Gates was concerned about playing with nature, she could not sit by and watch species become extinct without acting.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.yaleclimateconnections.org/2016/06/horrifying-research-seeks-to-save-hawaii-coral-reefs/|title='Horrifying' research seeks to save Hawaii reefs » Yale Climate Connections|date=2016-06-28|work=Yale Climate Connections|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> In 2016, Gates was named by [[Hawaii Business]] as one of the top 20 leaders of Hawaii.<ref name=":2"/> She explored whether non-super corals could be encouraged to take on new symbionts to improve their ability to withstand high temperatures.<ref name=":03">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2016/04/18/a-radical-attempt-to-save-the-reefs-and-forests|title=A Radical Attempt to Save the Reefs and Forests|last=Kolbert|first=Elizabeth|date=2016-04-18|magazine=The New Yorker|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> If Gates' project is successful, it could save the US$9.9 trillion.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/business/article/2149588/saving-worlds-coral-avert-wipeout-irreversible-costs|title=Saving the world's coral to avert a wipeout of irreversible costs|work=South China Morning Post|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> In 2018, the foundation supported a coral reef map, that allowed scientists to monitor corals in unprecedented detail.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.planet.com/pulse/planet-paul-g-allen-coral-map/|title=Planet, Paul G. Allen Philanthropies, & Leading Scientists Team Up to Map & Monitor World's Corals in Unprecedented Detail|website=www.planet.com|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref>

=== Public engagement ===
In addition to her career in research, Gates served as a mentor, public speaker, science communicator, and proponent for change and progress in the field of marine science.<ref name=":6"/> She captivated and inspired audiences with her passion, optimism, and, as she modestly put it, her English boarding school accent.<ref name=":6"/> She was elected the first female president of the [[International Society for Reef Studies]] in 2015 and significantly increased membership and involvement while she served.<ref name=":6"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://coralreefs.org/society-organisation/officers-and-members-of-council/|title=Officers & Councilors – International Society for Reef Studies|website=coralreefs.org|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> The ''Super Coral'' proposals were featured in ''[[Fast Company (magazine)|Fast Company]]'', [[Gizmodo]], [[PBS]], ''[[Newsweek]]'', ''[[Hawaii Business]]'', ''[[National Geographic]]'', the ''[[Huffington Post]]'', ''[[New Scientist]]'' and the [[BBC]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg23030680-600-im-creating-supercharged-corals-to-beat-climate-change/|title=I'm creating supercharged corals to beat climate change|last=Schiffman|first=Richard|work=New Scientist|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fastcompany.com/90188094/scientists-are-speeding-up-evolution-to-build-climate-change-resistance|title=Scientists are speeding up evolution to build climate change resistance|date=2018-07-18|access-date=2018-10-28|website=fastcompany.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oceantoday.noaa.gov/fullmoon-scienceofsupercorals/welcome.html|title=The Science of Super Corals – Coral Comeback|website=oceantoday.noaa.gov|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsweek.com/super-coral-reefs-climate-change-462172|title=Climate-adapted "super coral" could help revive the world's ailing reefs|date=2016-05-22|work=Newsweek|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=Super Coral That Can Survive Global 29, 2016|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bbc.com/earth/story/20160322-the-women-with-a-controversial-plan-to-save-corals|title=The women with a controversial plan to save corals|last=Riley|first=Alex|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hawaiibusiness.com/hawaiis-super-coral/|title=Hawaii's Super Coral: Evolution on Fast Forward|date=2018-09-12|work=Hawaii Business Magazine|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> Her work was featured in the [[Netflix]] documentary ''[[Chasing Coral]]''.<ref name=":7">{{Cite member of the [[Tetiaroa]] Society.<ref name=":32"/>

=== ''Chasing Coral'' ===
Gates' work at the Hawaiʻi Institute of Marine Biology is featured in the captivating Netflix documentary, ''[[Chasing Coral]]''.<ref name=":7"/> In the documentary, she explains her amazement with corals: "I have the utmost respect for corals because I think they have got us all fooled. Simplicity on the outside does not mean simplicity on the inside."<ref name=":7"/> The documentary showcases her work with Richard Vevers and the rest of his diving team on a project to capture the process of coral bleaching in the wild for the first time.<ref name=":7"/> Gates provides the scientific foundation of knowledge for the conduction of this project, educating the team of divers and the audience of the film throughout.<ref name=":7"/> She warns the audience of the "eradication of an entire ecosystem in our lifespan" to encourage progress in the movement against climate change.<ref name=":7"/> Her appearance in Chasing Coral was one of Gates' several efforts of public outreach and engagement, working to raise awareness of coral bleaching and inspire the public to put a stop to these events.<ref>{{Cite web |title=In The Story Of Dying Coral Reefs, A Call To Action |url=https://www.sciencefriday.com/segments/chasing-coral-movie/ |access-date=2023-07-03 |website=Science Friday |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Gates was born in Akrotiri, Cyprus, the sister of Timothy Gates and the daughter of John Amos Gates (RAF) and Muriel Peel Gates (physiotherapist).<ref name=":6"/> Her wife was Robin Burton-Gates, whom she married in September 2018. In her free time, she was an accomplished scuba diver, earned a black belt in karate, and started a school for karate in Hawaii.<ref name=":6"/>

Gates was diagnosed with [[brain cancer]] at 56 years old,<ref>[https://www.civilbeat.org/2018/10/rip-ruth-gates-the-world-loses-a-top-coral-scientist-and-indomitable-spirit/ RIP Ruth Gates: The World Loses A Top Coral Scientist And ‘Indomitable Spirit’], ''[[Honolulu Civil Beat]]'', October 30, 2018.</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Yong |first=Ed |date=2018-10-29 |title=The Fight for Corals Loses Its Great Champion |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2018/10/optimist-who-believed-saving-corals/574240/ |url-status=live |access-date=2018-10-29 |work=The Atlantic}}</ref> but died from complications during a surgery for [[diverticulitis]], unrelated to her former diagnosis.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2018/11/05/obituaries/ruth-gates-dead-marine-biologist-who-championed-coral.html Ruth Gates, Who Made Saving Coral Reefs Her Mission, Is Dead at 56], ''[[The New York Times]]'', November 5, 2018.</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/11/05/obituaries/ruth-gates-dead-marine-biologist-who-championed-coral.html|title=Ruth Gates, Who Made Saving Coral Reefs Her Mission, Is Dead at 56|last=Seelye|first=Katharine Q.|date=2018-11-05|work=The New York Times|access-date=2019-01-03}}</ref> Gates leaves a legacy of optimism and progress in the field of marine science: Van Oppen, the Gates Coral Lab, and multiple other labs across the globe, continue to study the mechanisms of resistance to climate change and how they may be passed down generations.<ref name=":6"/>
